_schema.description: Local commit review metadata for a VS Code extension. Each entry in 'reviews' represents a comment left by the user on a specific file and line at the time of a commit. Comments are intended to be addressed by an AI agent. The snapshot field captures surrounding code context at the time the comment was made so the agent can understand the original intent even if the code has since changed. The agent should check this file before starting any task and address all open comments.

fields.commitHash: Full git commit hash the comment was made against
fields.file: Relative path to the file from the repo root
fields.line: First line number of the selection at the time of the commit (1-based)
fields.lineEnd: Last line number of the selection; equals line for single-line comments
fields.side: 'right' = new (post-commit) file side; 'left' = old (pre-commit) file side
fields.body: The review comment text written by the user
fields.author: Who wrote the comment — 'reviewer' for the user, any string for agent replies

values.open: User has left a comment or question for the agent to address
values.in-progress: Agent is actively working on this comment
values.needs-input: Ball is in the user's court — either the agent has a question, or the agent answered a user question
values.addressed: Agent has finished — user should confirm or reopen
values.resolved: User confirmed the agent's work is acceptable
values.dismissed: User decided no action is needed
values.outdated: Agent detected the code has changed enough that the comment may no longer apply. See resolvedNote for details. User should reopen or dismiss.

fields.createdAt: ISO 8601 timestamp when the comment was first created
fields.addressedAt: ISO 8601 timestamp when the agent marked it addressed, null otherwise
fields.addressedByCommit: Full hash of the commit where the agent fixed the issue, null otherwise
fields.codeSnippet: Plain-text copy of the target line(s) at the time of the comment, for quick reference
fields.resolvedNote: Written by the agent when updating status. For 'resolved'/'addressed': what was changed. For 'outdated': what changed in the code. For 'pending': the agent's question for the user. Null if status is 'open'.

thread.description: Ordered list of follow-up messages after the initial comment body

items.author: Who wrote this reply ('reviewer' for the user, any string for the agent)

snapshot.description: Code context captured at the time of the comment. Use this to understand the original code the comment refers to regardless of how the file has changed since. Compare against the current file state to determine if the comment is still relevant. Each entry has 'line' (1-based line number) and 'content' (the line text).
snapshot.before: Up to 3 lines immediately preceding the target line
snapshot.target: The specific line or lines the comment is about
snapshot.after: Up to 3 lines immediately following the target line

reviews.body: I'm just adding this as a way to test what will happen.
reviews.author: reviewer

thread.author: reviewer
thread.body: You can close this when you see this.

reviews.resolvedNote: Closing as requested — this was a test comment.

thread.author: agent
thread.body: `STATUS_LABELS` is a lookup map from comment status values (e.g. `'open'`, `'resolved'`) to human-readable display strings (e.g. `'Open'`, `'Resolved'`). It's used when rendering status badges or labels in the UI so the display text can differ from the internal status key.

reviews.body: Where are these types being stored?
reviews.author: reviewer

thread.author: agent
thread.body: `CommentSnapshot` and `SnapshotLine` are defined at the top of `src/CommentManager.ts` (lines 15–24) and exported from there. `CommentSnapshot` has `before`, `target`, and `after` arrays of `SnapshotLine` objects (`{ line: number, content: string }`). They're used as a field on `ReviewComment` and stored in `.vscode/commit-reviews.json` under the `snapshot` key.

reviews.body: What does the ?? mean and why null instead of undefined?
reviews.author: reviewer

thread.author: agent
thread.body:
`??` is the **nullish coalescing operator** — it returns the right-hand side when the left-hand side is `null` or `undefined`, and the left-hand side otherwise. So `params.snapshot ?? null` means: use `params.snapshot` if it was provided, otherwise fall back to `null`.

`null` is used instead of `undefined` because `snapshot` is typed as `CommentSnapshot | null` on the `ReviewComment` interface. The key reason is JSON serialization: `undefined` properties are silently dropped when `JSON.stringify` runs, so the `snapshot` key would be missing from the saved file entirely. Using `null` keeps the field present and explicit in the JSON, which makes the data easier to work with (e.g. no need to guard against missing keys when reading the file).
